subject: math
cluster: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable
intro: This worksheet builds from computing a single measure of center or spread on small clean data sets, through ordering data and computing standard deviation, to comparing two distributions and choosing the appropriate statistic from the shape of each.

items.prompt: Find the mean of the data set $\{5, 8, 11, 12, 14\}$.

steps: There are $n = 5$ values, so divide: $\bar{x} = \dfrac{50}{5} = 10$.
The mean is $10$.

items.prompt: The list $\{3, 6, 9, 14, 20\}$ is already ordered from least to greatest. Find the median.

steps: With $n = 5$ values (odd), the median is the single middle value.
The middle position is the $3\text{rd}$ of $5$ values.
The $3\text{rd}$ value in $\{3, 6, 9, 14, 20\}$ is $9$, so the median is $9$.

items.prompt: A box plot of test scores shows $Q_1 = 68$ and $Q_3 = 85$. Find the interquartile range (IQR).

steps: The IQR is the spread of the middle half of the data: $\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1$.
Substitute: $\text{IQR} = 85 - 68$.
$\text{IQR} = 17$.

items.prompt: Find the mean of the data set $\{12, 18, 21, 25\}$.

steps: Add the values: $12 + 18 + 21 + 25 = 76$.
There are $n = 4$ values, so divide: $\bar{x} = \dfrac{76}{4} = 19$.
The mean is $19$.

items.prompt: A five-number summary is: minimum $= 4$, $Q_1 = 10$, median $= 15$, $Q_3 = 22$, maximum $= 30$. Find the IQR.

steps: The IQR uses the quartiles, not the minimum and maximum: $\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1$.
Substitute: $\text{IQR} = 22 - 10$.
$\text{IQR} = 12$. (Note: $\text{max} - \text{min} = 26$ is the range, not the IQR.)

items.prompt: Order the data set $\{9, 4, 7, 2, 10, 5\}$ and find its median.

steps: First order the values from least to greatest: $\{2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 10\}$.
With $n = 6$ values (even), the median is the mean of the two middle values, the $3\text{rd}$ and $4\text{th}$.
Those are $5$ and $7$, so the median is $\dfrac{5 + 7}{2} = \dfrac{12}{2} = 6$.

items.prompt: For the ordered data set $\{3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, 17\}$, find $Q_1$, $Q_3$, and the IQR.

steps: There are $n = 8$ values. Split into a lower half $\{3, 5, 7, 9\}$ and an upper half $\{11, 13, 15, 17\}$.
$Q_1$ is the median of the lower half: $\dfrac{5 + 7}{2} = 6$.
$Q_3$ is the median of the upper half: $\dfrac{13 + 15}{2} = 14$.

items.prompt: Compute the population standard deviation of the data set $\{2, 4, 6, 8\}$. Give the exact value and a decimal rounded to two places.

steps: Find the mean: $\bar{x} = \dfrac{2 + 4 + 6 + 8}{4} = \dfrac{20}{4} = 5$.
Find each deviation from the mean and square it: $(2-5)^2 = 9$, $(4-5)^2 = 1$, $(6-5)^2 = 1$, $(8-5)^2 = 9$.
Sum the squared deviations: $9 + 1 + 1 + 9 = 20$.
Divide by $n = 4$ to get the variance: $\dfrac{20}{4} = 5$.
Take the square root: $\sigma = \sqrt{5} \approx 2.24$.

items.prompt: A dot plot of daily high temperatures has most values bunched at the low end with a long tail stretching toward the high values. Identify the shape of the distribution (symmetric, skewed left, or skewed right), and name the pair of statistics (center and spread) best suited to describe it.
items.answer: Skewed right; use the median and IQR.

steps: Skew is named by the direction of the long tail. The tail stretches toward the high (right) end, so the distribution is skewed right.
For skewed data, the mean is pulled toward the long tail and the standard deviation is inflated by it.
The median and IQR are resistant to skew, so they best describe the center and spread of a skewed-right distribution.

items.prompt: Compute the population standard deviation of the data set $\{10, 12, 14, 16, 18\}$. Give the exact value and a decimal rounded to two places.

steps: Sum the squared deviations: $16 + 4 + 0 + 4 + 16 = 40$.
Divide by $n = 5$: $\dfrac{40}{5} = 8$.
Take the square root: $\sigma = \sqrt{8} = 2\sqrt{2} \approx 2.83$.

items.prompt: The data set $\{8, 9, 9, 10, 54\}$ contains an outlier. Compute both the mean and the median, then state which one better represents the center and explain why.
items.answer: Mean $= 18$, median $= 9$; the median better represents the center because the outlier $54$ inflates the mean.

steps: Median: the data is ordered and $n = 5$, so the median is the $3\text{rd}$ value, which is $9$.
The value $54$ is far larger than the others, so it is an outlier that pulls the mean up to $18$, well above the bulk of the data near $8$ to $10$.
The median ($9$) is resistant to the outlier and sits among the typical values, so it better represents the center.

items.prompt: Two roughly symmetric data sets of monthly rainfall (in cm) are compared. Set A has mean $30$ and standard deviation $\sigma_A = 2.5$. Set B has mean $30$ and standard deviation $\sigma_B = 6.0$. The means are equal. Which set is more consistent (less spread out), and how do you know?
items.answer: Set A is more consistent because its smaller standard deviation ($2.5 < 6.0$) means its values cluster more tightly around the mean.

steps: Both sets are roughly symmetric, so the standard deviation is the appropriate measure of spread.
Spread is measured by $\sigma$, not by the size of the center; equal means tell us nothing about variability.
Compare the standard deviations: $\sigma_A = 2.5$ and $\sigma_B = 6.0$, so $2.5 < 6.0$.
A smaller standard deviation means the values cluster more tightly around the mean, so Set A is more consistent.

items.prompt: Class A's quiz scores are summarized by a box plot that is roughly symmetric with median $80$ and IQR $10$. Class B's scores are strongly skewed right with median $74$, mean $81$ (pulled up by a few very high scores), and IQR $9$. Which class had the higher typical score, and which statistic should you compare to decide? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Class A; compare medians ($80 > 74$) because Class B is skewed and its mean is inflated by the high outliers.

steps: Choose the appropriate center for each shape. Class B is strongly skewed right, so its mean ($81$) is pulled up by the high scores and is not a reliable typical value; the median is resistant to skew.
To compare fairly across both classes, use the resistant statistic, the median, for both.
Compare medians: Class A has median $80$ and Class B has median $74$, and $80 > 74$.
So Class A had the higher typical score. (Comparing the inflated mean $81$ would wrongly favor Class B.)

items.prompt:
Two data sets are given as raw data:
Set P $= \{20, 22, 24, 26, 28\}$
Set Q $= \{20, 22, 24, 26, 88\}$
For each set decide whether the mean/standard deviation or the median/IQR better describes it, then compare the two sets' centers using the statistic appropriate to each. Justify using the shape.
items.answer: Set P is symmetric, so use mean $= 24$. Set Q has the outlier $88$, so use median $= 24$. Both typical centers are $24$, but Set Q is far more spread out because of the outlier.

steps: Set P $\{20, 22, 24, 26, 28\}$ is symmetric with no outliers, so the mean and standard deviation are appropriate. Mean $= \dfrac{20+22+24+26+28}{5} = \dfrac{120}{5} = 24$.
Set Q $\{20, 22, 24, 26, 88\}$ has an extreme outlier ($88$), so the resistant median and IQR are appropriate. Ordered, the median is the $3\text{rd}$ value, $24$.
Comparing centers with the statistic appropriate to each, both typical centers equal $24$, so the sets have the same typical value.

For spread, the outlier $88$ makes Set Q far more variable: its range is $88 - 20 = 68$ versus $28 - 20 = 8$ for Set P, and its standard deviation would be greatly inflated. So Set Q is much more spread out even though the centers match.

items.prompt:
A teacher records homework completion times (in minutes) for two study groups:
Group 1 $= \{15, 18, 20, 22, 25\}$
Group 2 $= \{16, 19, 21, 23, 95\}$
Write a complete comparison: for each group choose and compute the appropriate measure of center and the appropriate measure of spread (using the median and IQR where an outlier is present), then state which group was typically faster and which was more consistent, referencing the shape of each set.
items.answer: Group 1 (symmetric): mean $= 20$, $\sigma = \sqrt{11.6} \approx 3.41$. Group 2 (outlier $95$): median $= 21$, $Q_1 = 17.5$, $Q_3 = 59$, IQR $= 59 - 17.5 = 41.5$. Group 1 was typically faster (lower center, $20 < 21$) and Group 2 is far less consistent because the outlier makes its IQR ($41.5$) enormous relative to Group 1's tight spread.

steps: Group 1 $\{15, 18, 20, 22, 25\}$ is roughly symmetric with no outliers, so use the mean and standard deviation. Mean $= \dfrac{15+18+20+22+25}{5} = \dfrac{100}{5} = 20$.
Group 1 spread: squared deviations from $20$ are $25, 4, 0, 4, 25$, summing to $58$; variance $= \dfrac{58}{5} = 11.6$, so $\sigma = \sqrt{11.6} \approx 3.41$ minutes (tightly clustered).
Group 2 $\{16, 19, 21, 23, 95\}$ has an extreme outlier ($95$), so use the resistant median and IQR. Ordered, the median is the $3\text{rd}$ value, $21$.

Group 2 spread: lower half $\{16, 19\}$ gives $Q_1 = \dfrac{16+19}{2} = 17.5$; upper half $\{23, 95\}$ gives $Q_3 = \dfrac{23+95}{2} = 59$, so $\text{IQR} = 59 - 17.5 = 41.5$, which is large because of the outlier.
Compare centers using each group's appropriate statistic: Group 1's typical time ($20$) is less than Group 2's median ($21$), so Group 1 was typically slightly faster.
Compare spreads: Group 1's values cluster tightly ($\sigma \approx 3.4$) while Group 2 is stretched by the $95$-minute outlier (much larger IQR), so Group 1 is far more consistent.
